tagline: Recipes and rituals for unhurried days

posts.title: Sourdough, Day Three: The Float Test Lies
content: Everyone tells you to trust the float test. My starter floated beautifully on Sunday and the loaf still came out like a discus.
What actually worked: watching the dome. When the starter peaks and just begins to fall, that is the window — float test or no float test.
Recipe below makes one loaf, 75% hydration, overnight cold proof.
comments: The discus era is real. Mine could stop a door.
Peak-and-fall is the way. Float test is astrology for bakers.

posts.title: The Pour-Over Ritual
content: Four minutes of doing exactly one thing. That is the entire appeal.
The recipe: 20 grams of coffee, 320 grams of water at 94 degrees, a slow spiral, and no phone within reach. The last rule matters more than the water temperature.

posts.title: Sunday Shakshuka for People Who Sleep In
content: This is a 12:30pm breakfast and it knows it. One pan, six eggs, and a jar of the good peppers you have been saving.
The only real instruction: let the sauce reduce further than feels reasonable before the eggs go in. Watery shakshuka has ruined more Sundays than rain.
comments: Made this today. The pepper jar advice is correct.

posts.title: Market Haul: What September Actually Tastes Like
content: The tomatoes are on their way out and the squash is moving in, and the market this week was the exact midpoint of that handover.
Came home with: the last decent tomatoes, two kinds of squash I cannot name, a bag of figs that did not survive the walk, and plans.

posts.title: Miso Mornings
content: A bowl of miso soup takes four minutes and fixes approximately everything. It has quietly replaced toast as the default breakfast here.
Keep dashi in the fridge, keep the miso by the stove, and do not boil it after the paste goes in. That is the whole technique.

drafts.title: Overnight Oats That Are Not Sad
content: Toasted oats, a pinch of salt, and one thing that crunches. That is the whole trick, and it took me three years to learn it.

drafts.title: Autumn Market Notes
content: Figs are in, the last of the peaches are out, and someone is already selling chestnuts. Too early. I bought some anyway.

drafts.title: Why I Stopped Buying Bread on Weekdays
content: The starter demanded a schedule and the schedule won. A loaf every Tuesday and Friday, and the bakery only on Sundays.
Photograph the plum jam before it is gone.
